original_question: For homogeneous structures whose current big-Ramsey-degree proofs rely on forcing, can those arguments be replaced by proofs that are entirely combinatorial, including for k-clique-free homogeneous graphs with k >= 4 and other free-amalgamation classes where current methods do not yet provide such proofs?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.2 in Section 6 ("For results whose proofs use the method of forcing, find new proofs which are purely combinatorial."), read with the Section 5.2 discussion of forcing-based big Ramsey results for free-amalgamation classes and Theorem 5.5.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's open problem about replacing forcing-based arguments by purely combinatorial ones, and it correctly singles out the k-clique-free homogeneous graphs for k >= 4 together with other free-amalgamation (FAP) classes as the main unresolved examples named in the paper.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation is Problem 6.2, whose wording is broader than the draft: it asks for new purely combinatorial proofs for all results in the area whose proofs use forcing, not only for some big-Ramsey-degree arguments.

The paper explicitly notes that the triangle-free homogeneous graph G_3 is no longer part of the open case, because Hubicka already gave a combinatorial proof; the unresolved Henson-graph cases are G_k for k >= 4.
The paper's standing convention is that 'homogeneous' means countably infinite homogeneous; that countability is implicit in the draft and should be made explicit in a stand-alone question.

In the nearby technical context, the forcing-based results arise from Halpern-Lauchli-style theorems on coding trees and concern the classes treated in Section 5.2, especially countable homogeneous structures K with finitely many relations of arity at most two and Age(K) = Forb(F) for a finite set F of finite irreducible structures.
If the question is to be fully stand-alone, FAP should be spelled out as 'free amalgamation property' (equivalently, the age is a free-amalgamation Fraisse class).
The draft says 'where current methods do not yet provide such proofs'; the paper's exact phrasing is that 'new methods will be needed,' which is the sharper paper-faithful formulation.

The nearby forcing-based results are stated in terms of big Ramsey structures as well as big Ramsey degrees, so restricting the question only to 'big-Ramsey-degree proofs' slightly narrows the paper's wording.
refined_question: Can one replace the existing forcing-based proofs for the big Ramsey results of the countable homogeneous free-amalgamation structures treated in Section 5.2 by proofs that are entirely combinatorial; in particular, can this be done for each Henson graph G_k (the countable homogeneous k-clique-free graph) with k >= 4, and for the other similar Fraisse limits whose ages have the free amalgamation property (FAP) and are currently handled by forcing? (The case G_3 is excluded, since a combinatorial proof is already known.)
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 6.2, not at a statement from the introduction. The decisive markers are the request to replace forcing by 'purely combinatorial' proofs and the explicit mention of k-clique-free homogeneous graphs with k >= 4. Section 5.2 explains that forcing enters through Halpern-Lauchli-style theorems for coding trees in free-amalgamation settings and culminates in forcing-based big Ramsey results such as Theorem 5.5. Section 6 then states the official open problem in exactly this direction and immediately clarifies that G_3 already has a combinatorial proof, while G_k for k >= 4 and other such FAP classes still require new methods.
